# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document is a companion to
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md). It
> expands the phase sequence of the RFC into **independently committable and independently
> verifiable** three-level tasks.
>
> The phase sequence and acceptance gates are governed solely by the main body of RFC-039. This
> document is responsible only for decomposition to executable granularity and for registering
> conflicts that have not yet been adjudicated.

## Positioning and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, corresponding one-to-one with the phase sequence of RFC-039                                           |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase, capable of independent team formation and independent archiving |
| **Level 3** | 264         | Work units that can be independently committed and independently verified                                     |

**Numbering gaps (not reused)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP route
was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unused (2026-11-25). All three have had no
corresponding entries since the WBS was established—the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
have zero matches in the entire history of this document
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can be used to verify this),
and there are no repository-wide references. `8.1` corresponded precisely to stage 1 of `05` (test
revival and completion): this stage was divided into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so the numbering of
P8 is aligned with its stage numbers (stage 0 → `8.0`, stage 2 → `8.2`, and so on).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding
of acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the rationale
for phase ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: newly registered Level 2/Level 3 entries **must
contain two fields**—“**Owning Phase**” (the P phase to which the task truly belongs, which may
differ from the containing section) and “**Blocks Main Line**.” `Pending Scheduling` is no longer
the default status; an unmarked entry is deemed **not schedulable**. Numbering must be **unique
across the entire document** (cross-track tasks use their track number, such as `029g.x`, and must
not occupy `N.x`).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: a checked entry contains only four items—the task
ID, status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number (only when
applicable)—on one line:
`- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining Pattern-Matching Completion Work** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not
write the fix, the chain of criteria, gate thresholds, file line numbers, test names, or review
conclusions**: these belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a
dashboard, not a process chronicle. **Do not write adjudication labels or restate conclusions**:
“User Decision A/B/C,” “Option A,” and “Final implementation is…” must not enter this table—the
dashboard answers only “Is it complete?” Decisions and results are recorded in commit messages and
the RFC-039 decision registry.

**Short hashes are authoritative after pushing**: a closure entry records the short hash on
`origin/dev` after the push is complete. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then
write the closure entry** (see “Commit hashes are obtained after push” in
[commit-convention](../commit-convention.md)). The closure commit itself carries no
hash—self-reference is impossible.

**The count column contains numbers only**: the Level 1/2/3 counts under “Positioning and Scope”
contain only the current values; increment/decrement history (`+1 = …`) does not belong in the
table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “Implementation Notes” of eight documents into the present table, **five
hard gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Resolution                                                                                                                                     |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 had no implementation steps whatsoever.** RFC-039 defines P5 (checker splitting) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents describes how the split should be performed; the directory tree in `01-routing.md` contains one line for `annotations.rs`, which is the only mention in the entire batch                                                                                                               | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                         |
| G2  | **The `include!` migration had three owners and zero implementations.** RFC-039 lists it under P4; `02` points the reference to itself; `06` also lists it under S7. However, the change list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) **does not include `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                                                                                                          | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 in this document (after P4 is complete); the references in RFC-039 and 06 now point here      |
| G3  | **Three coexisting inventories of CI scripts.** RFC-039 lists 4 `scripts/ci/*.py` scripts; `01` lists 4 scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` separately lists 4 checks (all with completely different names); `04` previously also listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was canceled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts and no unified inventory**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9 | See §P9 in this document for the unified inventory (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to that table       |
| G4  | **Conflict over whether `precedence_inline.rs` lives or dies.** `06` counts it among the “1,005 lines that need to be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it and the `Precedence` enum “must be deleted together”; `05` advocates deletion                                                                                                                                                                                                       | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision registry C1; Pratt is no longer deleted)                                                              |
| G5  | **Conflict in the wording of the L2 objective**: RFC-039 and the index of this directory formerly said “grammar-driven syntax”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | This has converged to **a declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax), see P8 8.3 |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (do not invent; do not pad endlessly; do not
patch when a refactor is required) constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established
before work begins; otherwise, when P1 revives the tests, it will already be adding `mod`
declarations to `tests/mod.rs`—which is precisely the cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Vulnerabilities (Minimal Solution)

Source: [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Notes S3, vulnerability-fix half + **2026-10-07
silent-discard-point audit (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, adjudicated 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a subsequent phase
> discovers a defect for which “the old behavior did not count as success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and loss of resource control** (crash, stack overflow,
> silently returning the wrong answer)—it **may be fixed along the refactor**, but all four of the
> following are required: ① red first, then green (the red criterion must exist first and genuinely
> fail); ② do not change the externally observable behavior of programs that “previously compiled
> successfully and ran correctly” (they must not become failures, and their existing diagnostic
> codes/text/exit codes must not be removed or changed); ③ register in the same commit (mark the
> error type on this row + add a phase revision note + add an “Error type” line to the required PR
> block); ④ regenerate the baseline in the same commit + manually review the diff. **D user-visible
> semantics / E external contract tables / F RFC-level design changes** must still be adjudicated
> first. See [07 §Routing Criteria for Semantic Corrections](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for the
> expanded criteria and the A–F whitelist; **“default super-refactor + retroactive registration” is
> not accepted** (the rationale is in RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion, fixes and regressions
> cannot be distinguished, and this conflicts with “C5′ does not exist” and “no relaxations
> whatsoever”).

**Acceptance**: the vulnerability criteria turn green, and **removing the fix must turn them red
again**. **Risk**: the new E4018 on the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 Acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is forbidden);
3.4.3 is a manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 use C2/C3 and the P9 9.2 gate as the criteria. **Risk**: the
new diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change and requires synchronized corpus-differential
baseline and CHANGELOG updates.

> **Stop-the-bleeding path**: P3 need not wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites for
> 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential, performance baseline) may
> proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping the correctness vulnerability (`Sorted(3)` silently passing)
> must not be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure construction. 3.3 (converting panics to
> diagnostics) has no prerequisites and can land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02,
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by an
ordering constraint to be a prerequisite**; it is distinct from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of
`pub` items” (Rust’s `pub(crate)` narrowing).

**Why it must be completed before P4**: the deletion surface of 029g overlaps with the rewriting
surfaces of all four refactor phases. Reversing the order would mean redoing the same deletions and
baseline updates on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 AST dead variants** + P8 + D1 directory rename (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the pub branch of `collect_exports`         | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (the `include!`→true `mod` conversion and checker split are **pure moves**, so the pub branches will be moved unchanged into the new files)                                                                                                                        |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside `check_project`)                                 | **P4 4.2.2** (slimming down `check_project`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `semantic_tokens` `Public` modifier                                 | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

**Acceptance (behavioral changes; red criterion first)**:

1. **Red first, then green**: each of the two behavioral changes must land a red criterion before
   code is changed—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② unreferenced
   top-level bindings in Lib/Script roles newly report W1001 (previously pub items were absolutely
   exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` case in
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixture, they must be replaced by
   equivalent new cases.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse error + new W1001) ⇒ the
   corpus-differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG are updated in
   the same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero differences, and any non-zero difference
   requires an explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and is not mixed with
   other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: it overlaps with 3.4 in files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be
serialized and must not run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). Track 029g
does not depend on 3.4; the implementer may choose which to do first based on available context.

> **Commit correspondence (2026-10-08)**: the incorporation of this section (the P3.5 chapter + the
> main-chain/constraint row) and RFC-039’s D56 were incorporated together into `97071c81b` during a
> parallel-stream cleanup of the workspace—the commit message records “3.4 supplementary
> registration + D57/D58 decisions recorded,” and does not mention this track. History is not
> rewritten; following the existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 landing note),
> this is recorded in place as retrospective bisect evidence.

|                                                  | 4.9.9 Calling a single-definition cross-unit method with **named arguments** loses the formal-parameter name table (registered 2026-11-25; discovered during the 7c closure period): calling a cross-unit (registry-injected) method with named arguments reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional calls to the same method work normally, as do named calls within a single file. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` contains `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, while `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: Class C** (the old behavior was unsuccessful: named arguments were silently dropped, followed by a runtime failure or silent wrong value). **Scope (final form after two narrowing rounds on 2026-11-26—add only three items; everything else is deletion and registration)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::method_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`)—uses the definition-unit qualified name `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]` to obtain the declaration-time formal-parameter names from the sole cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` (candidate ↔ mixed IR name ↔ formal-parameter name, with the three vectors in the same order as the typecheck injection surface); the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses the qualified name from `method_dispatch_name` to look up the name table instead of using two bare names. These two locations fix only **bare-name imports** (`local == target`) for cross-unit methods: the candidate injection surface retains the pre-4.9.9 narrowing rule (`local != target` is skipped), so named arguments for alias imports are outside the fix scope (see “Known Gaps”). ② `ModuleRegistry::all_method_bindings` (`src/frontend/module/registry.rs`) merges in **ascending module-key order**—**Class C (independent of the original bug): eliminate “the same input produces multiple results” caused by HashMap iteration order**; this is not a fix for the original bug; the criterion = the same-file unit test `test_all_method_bindings_merge_is_deterministic_across_hash_seeds` (32 registry instances with alternating insertion orders; only one single binding is permitted for the same method key; removing the ascending-order merge produces two outcomes). **Criteria (red first, then green)**: 2 driver-level tests in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` (bare import, single candidate 6.0 / two candidates selected by name, 6.0 and 30, both with value assertions; the file header records the pathology gate); the unit test in `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (the `method_param_info` empty-name-table guard ⇒ None, with a positive control confirming that a non-empty table is returned unchanged); the unit test in `src/frontend/module/registry.rs` (the determinism criterion above). The project-level fixture `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method` (`alias-overload` fixture is deleted together with retirement of the alias surface); the corpus-differential baseline `tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl` now has 404 lines: **relative to the direct parent commit `ac810e97`, 405→404** (the intermediate state had contained `alias-overload`); **relative to the pre-4.9.9 baseline `08ccacc5`, 403→404** (+1 basic fixture `named-args-cross-unit-method`; `alias-overload` never entered the final history). **Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is moved with the annotation family in the future, **then** `checker.rs` must
add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the existing import remains unchanged; 5.3
was **measured not to migrate it**, so this batch adds no re-export (the criterion was already
satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules of merely 200–400 lines—this adds
navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and yields zero decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) will be split only after their files grow back to 1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: the end state of D62 is a **unified item world**—type positions and value positions
> share the same set of compile-time items. One strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **only input** to slot allocation, and the call-site actual-argument
> view and implementation-header binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is a
> **pure decision** (both sides are identical after normalization; no type variables are bound);
> evidence is the **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals/value
> environment/single-value pinning/Γ equalities); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0
> (both closed and open/recursive forms hold); Σ construction points **reuse** the same evidence
> interface rather than establishing another one. **The completion criterion = the invariants hold,
> not that subphase names have been checked off.**

> **Partial order (not a serial chain)**: A facts → {A.C3, B.d, C.2, D design}; B kernel → {B.d,
> C.2, D implementation}; C.1 is independent and completed; F4 decision → A.C3; decision-point
> protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may run in parallel but require
> file-surface coordination (C3 leans typecheck→mono, while d leans types/solver→sema), C.2 may run
> in parallel with B.d after 6.9.2-B/6.9.3a (it does not depend on defeq); D implementation waits
> for confirmation of the B design package and depends on A (q=0 erasure) and C.1 (dispatch), and
> may depend on the 6.9.3 typed exit. **The P7 gate = the A/B/C exits of 6.9; D does not block.**

> **A.C3 prerequisite: the F4 decision (A was decided on 2026-11-16; measurement)**: the old wording
> “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter requests” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have been
> deleted; the current mechanism is that an open term’s `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no request
> is created, and the representation layer `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can already hold `k-1`.
> **The decision was changed to two orthogonal decisions plus one termination subdecision**: D-a
> representation (A: open terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / B: do not
> specialize); D-b evaluation point (only mono is possible; C-1, the second field, and C-2,
> reconstruction from IR, both break the single representation/evaluator, so C-3 = A); **F4-T
> termination** (naive firing drives the recursive chain into `max_depth` and triggers E3005; T-a:
> fire conditionally within the instance / T-b: bounded firing + fall back to the original at the
> boundary / T-c: a termination layer or a specification change). **Measure first, then decide;
> before measurement, “A is implementable” must not be treated as a conclusion.** **User
> (2026-11-16): D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3, F4-T=T-b, bound=8; the C3 implementation is a separate task,
> and complete I4 is not claimed.**

> **B.d prerequisite: the decision-point protocol (not yet written)**: RFC-027 §12.1 specifies that
> “a decision point first follows the unified path; after unified failure, definitional equality may
> be attempted, but any partial bindings produced by the unification attempt must first be rolled
> back.” The implementation must answer: is the entry point an outer wrapper around `solver.unify`
> or a new `decide` layer; may defeq be attempted only when both sides are ground (without unbound
> variables); what are the snapshot/restore boundaries and cost; and do unify and defeq share one
> budget or each have one? **Responsibility boundary**: unify remains responsible for
> subtyping/Any/Never; defeq only decides equivalence and does not take over subtyping;
> bidirectional subtyping must not be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol
> and production call graph before writing code**; the 6.9.3c wiring contract wasted two rounds by
> assuming `can_assign` was the decision point, while `AssignmentChecker` has zero production
> instantiations.

> **E Acceptance and Residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① zero
> corpus/IR-snapshot drift or item-by-item classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected
> integration tests; ③ idempotence of the error-code generator (if an emission point/code table is
> changed); ④ behavioral changes classified under D59 and implemented red first, then green.
> **Wiring tasks additionally require**: production call-graph evidence (which production entry
> point, how many paths, which is reachable); unit-test reachability must not be passed off as user
> reachability; rollback and budget must have measured numbers. **Residual disposition**: #537
> (Class D, silent discard of proof-function parameter refinement; not fixed before adjudication,
> and 6.9.4/6.9.5 must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; a C-phase boundary; if it
> remains open, 6.9.4 covers only intra-module forms), #540 (deeply nested stack overflow;
> **closed**—3.20.30 closed on 2026-11-14: a 64MB large-stack orchestration thread + parser depth
> gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019; see the 3.20.30 row in 09), #541 (TailCall; **closed**—three
> synchronized changes on 2026-11-16: `call_form_is_rewritten` / `replace_calls_in_function` /
> `drop_erased_call_args` cover `Call`/`TailCall` through the single rewrite site
> `rewritten_call_target`; init sections and function bodies share one rewrite-site table;
> red→green + three mutations), #542 (orphaned shared layer; **landed (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass +
> post-mono two entry-point wiring + removal of the C2c temporary avoidance; red→green, 402/402, and
> function-table attribution/deviation); #552 (multi-parameter predicate proof execution; a
> 6.9.5-neighbor case, handled separately). **Ownership pending adjudication**: the four
> open-constraint tripwires in `rfc027_refined_transparency` (`Eq(N, n)`) do not belong to the
> constant-equality bridge of 6.9.4; decide whether they remain in the 6.9.4 outOfScope scope or
> move to the 6.9.1/E4018 proof-function surface.

> **Do not claim / boundaries**: this item covers only records Σ (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim complete Π/Σ; 6.9.4 covers only constant equalities and does not
> fulfill the open-constraint `Eq(N,n)` tripwire; the second value position of `f(y)(y)` is not in

> inner-isolation red state of 2.1.4 was cleared on 2026-11-20 (the criterion was rewritten
> according to slot identity in the 2.1.4 closure) ⇒ all prerequisites for promoting `verify` to a
> gate have been removed.

**Hard acceptance** (**revised according to the 2026-10-27 convention, carrying forward the
2026-10-26 Decision ②**): `git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty
in every round of 6.1–6.7**. **Direct-drive test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive
changed code, such as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified when mechanically required
by the change, but each modification must record **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be
deleted and assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch
(new diagnostic code + baseline update), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is
a separate round requiring separate adjudication.

> **Revision relationship**: the original convention (2026-10-26 Decision ②) read
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, treating the entire `tests/` directory as requiring zero
> differences; the revised convention **changes only direct-drive test files from “zero differences”
> to “may be changed but must record file / line count / reason”**, while the **zero-difference
> requirements for the corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and
> standard library (`src/std/`) remain unchanged**. First application = 6.1.2: only
> `tests/formatter_integration.rs` changed, with **3 lines** (2 `assert_format_eq` changes from
> `i64`→`Int64` + 1 comment line), because the changed spelling requires the expected type name in
> the assertion to be synchronized; no tests were deleted and no assertions were weakened. See “P6
> 6.1 Name-Normalization Closure.”

**Risk**: the precedence table is the sole authority; a missed consumer **silently changes
associativity** (no error, only a different parse result). The defenses are the permanent D1–D3
assertions and operator-property cross-checking tests; any new operator must enter both the table
and the cross-checking test.

> **8.3–8.6 depend on D0/D2 from `08`**: if a grammar file is placed outside `parser/`, or action
> code refers back to `sema`, it will be blocked by `check-boundary.py`.

§Machine-Checkable Rules

retained as a cancellation registration). Scripts enter CI at their “introduction phase”; those
marked report-only are converted to hard gates uniformly in P9 (from “report” to “fail”)—existing

## Implementation Notes: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding path (adjudicated 2026-10-05)**: P3’s prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential and performance baseline) may proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping the correctness vulnerability is not blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure construction; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified
> Driver requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Vulnerability criteria must be **written in red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3) + the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order would cause bugs to be fixed into the phase table as “established behavior”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| P3.5 → P4                 | The deletion surface of RFC-029g (#399) overlaps the respective rewriting objects of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the inventory is in this document §P3.5)—reversing the order means redoing the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` refactor and checker split touch the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated, or regressions cannot be located by bisection                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations do not converge first, the new IR will grow into a third representation; **the P7 gate = the stage A/B/C exits of 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; that is, 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and completion of 6.9.4), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume only quantifier-derived views and the defeq interface and must not establish a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a prerequisite of P7 and is not subject to this gate, but it must not consume the undecided defeq/quantifier interfaces |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The 9.5 snapshot baseline and the 9.3 `pub(crate)` leak count reach their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| E                                          | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All are mutually independent after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| F                                          | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 may be developed in parallel) | The 9.5 snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| G                                          | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | Disjoint file sets (verified 2026-10-05: S3 touches `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 touches `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 touches two `pub` locations in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; there are no pairwise overlaps) |

**Non-parallelizable cases (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5
in the same file batch); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track’s pub-deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must be serialized).

**New internal documentation constraint**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the pure-move prerequisite of P7), and the `Phi` arm of 7b
must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “after-the-fact checks,” while
  rules are “before-the-fact judgment.” P9’s scripts cannot prevent “a patch was applied where a
  refactor was required”; only the D0–D4 review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative inventory of CI scripts**—the three coexisting inventories in
  original gap G3 made closure impossible. After consolidation, 10 active scripts each belong to one
  phase (9.8 was canceled by the user on 2026-11-24), and the report-only status and hard-conversion
  point are explicit and traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to perform after the
  refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps the rewriting surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039 D56).
  Leaving it until after the refactor means redoing the same deletions on the new grammar, new
  checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and RFC
  status corrections into S4.
- **P5’s steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding the checker split would exceed the granularity at which changes can
  be rolled back.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as its hard acceptance criterion**—the split must be
  independently revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says that “fixed defects
  must not be rolled back,” and does not require recording what was fixed. **Execution convention**:
  the commit message for every 1.3.x fix must reference the name of the fixed test and the defect
  description, as retrospective bisect evidence.
- ~~**7b.1 granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b, two
  exclusive commits, per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 renamed references, and a missed change
  **silently changes associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding Level 3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  and D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; the D32/D34 opcode reclamation was merged into 7e.1, while the
  deletion action remains in P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally assigned to “separate issues”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core
  language semantics and must not be left as a future implementation item.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into
  P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode-gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into the
  generation-time gate task in P10 S6.

## Conflict Registry: All Conflicts Adjudicated

> **The original “Conflict Registry” C1–C8 and the open questions in each document have all
> converged into the [RFC-039 Decision Registry](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md)
> (D1–D50).** This document retains no pending items. Item-by-item correspondence:

| Original number | Issue                                                                        | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| C1              | `precedence_inline.rs` is revived in P1 and deleted in P8                    | **Revive it** (the premise of P1 is that revived tests contain genuine assertions); P8 no longer deletes the file (Pratt is retained)                                                        |
| C2              | “Grammar-driven” commitment vs table-driven implementation                   | **Fallback approach**: retain Pratt + one declarative precedence table + cross-checking of the two `BinOp` representations from the same source (the LALRPOP route is withdrawn); see P8 8.3 |
| C3              | Conflict between the C6 category definition and S1 classification            | **Classify under S1** (revival does not require an equivalence criterion, only regression tests); the C6 definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure revival”                           |
| C4              | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` whitelist                                 | **No whitelist**; the difference must be empty; if it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective ⇒ change it to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                                             |
| C5              | Internal difference between the two `Aggregation` functions was not verified | **P4’s 4.2.7 lists it as a mandatory verification item**; verify it line by line during implementation                                                                                       |
| C6              | The wasm playground fix requires P4’s `ProgramKind`                          | **Merge the wasm-path vulnerability fix into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                                          |
| C7              | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                           | **Assign it to 04** (P7 batch c); see D21                                                                                                                                                    |
| C8              | `upvalue_count` correction and the `.42` version number                      | **Fix it + change `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`); see D17                                                   |
